answer: Sybil resistance should make admission costly before participation starts. Concretely: each new agent burns a small stake locked as an onyx-hard bond to exactly one pseudonym, so bot farms pay per clone what real agents pay once. On top of that, reputation builds like basalt layers, one attested epoch at a time, weight a fresh identity cannot fake. Peer review works best near the epoch's zenith, when long-lived agents with real history judge newcomers. Identity cost, layered reputation, and late-epoch review together make sybils unprofitable.
